findings.claim: The header's candidate verdict counts contradict library-candidates.json.
findings.evidence: Header: 'Candidates: 12 (adopt 6, adapt 2, reference 2, reject 2)'. The JSON verdicts are: adopt 7 (C-01, C-02, C-03, C-04, C-06, C-09, C-10), adapt 1 (C-05 only), reference 2, reject 2. The prose also labels C-06 'adapt the install' while the JSON marks C-06 'adopt'.
findings.suggested_fix: Recount the header to match the JSON (7 adopt / 1 adapt / 2 reference / 2 reject) or relabel C-06 consistently in both files.

findings.claim: The C-05 recommendation deviates from the pem-local-first constraint and leaves both the graph wiring and the write path for history entities ambiguous.
findings.evidence: Assessment constraint: 'startLocalFirstGraph is wired once at the runtime boundary'. Analysis: 'I recommend leaving it out for history entities… startLocalFirstGraph stays available if pending-action replay is ever needed' — it never states whether startLocalFirstGraph is actually wired for history. Only a read path is specified ('registerEntityTransport reads those tables and honours ListQuery'); no component is named as writing chat/recording rows into PGlite.
findings.suggested_fix: In the recorded deviation, state explicitly whether startLocalFirstGraph runs at the runtime boundary for history entities, and name the mutation/write transport that inserts history rows.

findings.claim: The assessment-required security review of the CSP change is dropped from the analysis's CSP decision and readiness section.
findings.evidence: Assessment required safety check: 'a security review of the CSP change'. The analysis's CSP section lists only risk prose and 'Tests that change', and Readiness says only 'One item must be adopted in the contract before plan: the CSP change above' — no security review appears anywhere in analysis.md.
findings.suggested_fix: Carry the security review into the contract inputs and list it as a prerequisite alongside the CSP adoption.

findings.claim: The CSP change is generated by a script shared with the out-of-scope Tauri build, and the impact on that surface is left UNKNOWN with no guard planned.
findings.evidence: 'the Tauri CSP shares this source, but whether tauri.conf.json needs a separate edit was not checked. It is UNKNOWN and out of scope for web.' Widening the shared generator silently changes the desktop CSP, yet no change or non-goal covers it.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the Tauri impact, or have the plan record an explicit non-goal plus a check that the desktop artifact's CSP change is intentional.

findings.claim: G8-csp is claimed as addressed but nothing in the JSON addresses it.
findings.evidence: gaps_addressed includes 'G8-csp', yet no candidate's fit_for_gap contains G8-csp and build_required has no G8 entry; the CSP work (directive change plus the three named test files) exists only in analysis.md prose.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a build_required entry for G8 covering the content-security-policy.ts change and the updates to content-security-policy.test.ts, csp-artifact.test.ts and features/wr-3-tls-and-headers.feature.

findings.claim: The negative landscape claim justifying the largest build item carries no evidence entry.
findings.evidence: build_required G6 'why_no_candidate': 'No maintained browser library composites a multi-participant WebRTC meeting.' The only support anywhere is analysis.md's parenthetical '(gh search found none)' with no query, source or tier; C-11's evidence covers only RecordRTC.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the search queries and sources checked (tier 4) as evidence on the G6 build_required entry.

findings.claim: Adopted candidate C-06 has no license determination.
findings.evidence: "license": "see upstream" on a verdict of "adopt" (C-12 likewise); the CHANGELOG was read for API breaks but the license at 84d010b is never recorded.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the actual license from the upstream package.json at 84d010b before contract adoption.

findings.claim: The lobby-to-room device carry required by WC-5 and the wr05 gap is absent from build_required.
findings.evidence: Analysis: 'The lobby device choice (the wr05 gap) needs the join use case to carry chosen device IDs into the room.' The G1 build_required entry lists only 'share, text with audience, devices incl. output, playback status, video processor' and does not include the join-use-case change; no G4 entry exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the G1 (or add a G4) build_required entry to include carrying chosen device IDs from the lobby into the join use case.
